The content and presentation of participant information sheets play a significant role in influencing recruitment and participation for an antenatal (pregnancy-related) intervention. Research suggests that the way information is presented can have a substantial impact on whether pregnant women are likely to engage with and participate in such interventions.

 Studies have shown that the clarity, simplicity, and relevance of the content, as well as the overall design of the participant information sheets, can influence recruitment and participation rates. For example, a study found that pregnant women who received information sheets with detailed explanations of the intervention were more likely to engage with it compared to those who received simpler or more straightforward information.

 Furthermore, some research indicates that the presentation of information may also play a role in influencing attitudes and perceptions towards the intervention. For instance, one study found that participant information sheets with images or videos could increase perceived relevance and effectiveness of the intervention, leading to increased participation rates.

It is essential to note, however, that the design and content of participant information sheets should be tailored to the specific needs and preferences of their target audience (in this case, pregnant women). A well-designed information sheet should be clear, concise, and engaging, with a clear call-to-action and easy navigation through the information.

Overall, incorporating feedback from pregnant women on the effectiveness of participant information sheets can help healthcare providers refine their design to better meet the needs of their target audience. This may involve pilot-testing different versions of the information sheet or gathering more data on how participants interact with and respond to different types of information materials. By taking a participatory approach to designing and disseminating antenatal interventions, healthcare providers may be able to increase participation rates and improve outcomes for pregnant women.

In summary, the content and presentation of participant information sheets are critical in influencing recruitment and participation for an antenatal intervention. A well-designed information sheet should be clear, concise, and engaging, with a clear call-to-action and easy navigation through the information. Providing feedback to pregnant women on the effectiveness of these materials can help healthcare providers refine their design and improve outcomes.
